wrapper_comparison.finding: The counterhypothesis partially survives: libportal is a viable thin session wrapper rather than an opaque media framework. It exposes screencast creation/start, session state, external close signal, restore-token lifecycle, raw stream GVariant a(ua{sv}), and the PipeWire remote fd. Because the raw stream property dictionary is retained, a v6 pipewire-serial can be read by the F2 adapter even though libportal's documentation still foregrounds the legacy node-id tuple member.
advantages: less custom D-Bus request/session lifecycle code
closed signal for external session shutdown
raw stream property dictionary remains available
restore token and persist mode are exposed
limitations: public API does not expose the portal D-Bus session object path directly; F2 must not pretend an adapter-local id is the native session handle
xdp_session_get_streams documentation still describes node-id plus properties and does not itself elevate pipewire-serial to a typed API field
libportal does not replace PipeWire buffer ingestion, F2 permission intersection, generation fences, bounded FrameRef fan-out or native-runtime acceptance
camera capture remains a distinct Camera portal path and must not be conflated with ScreenCast

proposed_f2_shape.name: LinuxPortalPipeWireCaptureAdapter/v0
logical_flow: create/select/start XDG ScreenCast session through libportal or exact protocol-equivalent adapter
read selected stream property dictionary and require pipewire-serial when portal v6 exposes it
construct HostPermissionGrant bound to exact adapter session instance + pipewire-serial + F2 source_generation
intersect HostPermissionGrant with requested F2 PerceptionCapabilitySnapshot
acquire existing F2 CaptureOwnerLease only after effective permission snapshot exists
connect PipeWire stream targeted by object.serial via PW_KEY_TARGET_OBJECT
dequeue native buffers and stamp F2 host monotonic capture time plus bounded native timing provenance
publish only bounded CaptureFrameRef metadata into existing RetinaCaptureBroker
on native invalidation stop ingestion before accepting another frame, release owner, invalidate host grant and advance source_generation before reopen

ephemeral_only: raw restore token unless the explicit product permission design later requires secure persistence
explicitly_noncanonical: PipeWire graph timing without clock mapping

identity_mapping.rule: External close or client/session loss invalidates current host grant and capture lease.
May remain stable across restoration; never sufficient to prove same concrete native stream instance.
Documented reuse makes stale-target ABA possible.
Bind to F2 source_generation and target with PW_KEY_TARGET_OBJECT; do not rename it to source_id.
Advance before any reopened/restored/replaced native stream instance can publish frames.

permission_mapping.native_success_condition: ScreenCast session successfully started and still ACTIVE, selected stream exists, PipeWire remote can be opened, stream instance identity is bound, and adapter has not observed a native invalidation event.
permission_mapping.host_grant_construction: Construct HostPermissionGrant only from observed native success plus F2-known source/generation. native_permission_ref must be an adapter-produced digest/reference over the observed session-state evidence and stream serial; it must not be a restore token or node id.
permission_mapping.effective_permission: Use existing resolve_effective_perception_snapshot(requested_snapshot, host_grant, now) so user/dashboard policy and native host permission are intersected rather than substituted.
permission_mapping.execution_recheck: Before accepting/publishing a buffer, require current adapter state ACTIVE, expected F2 generation, expected pipewire-serial and non-invalidated HostPermissionGrant; otherwise fail closed before FrameRef publication.

generation_invalidation_matrix.event: creating D-Bus client disappears or portal connection is lost
PipeWire stream enters ERROR/UNCONNECTED after active binding
selected stream pipewire-serial changes or required serial no longer resolves
restore attempt succeeds with same portal stream id but a new pipewire-serial
restore token exists but restore fails or permission was withdrawn

timing_mapping.clock_rule: Do not compare or merge PipeWire graph/cycle time with F2 host monotonic time as if they were the same domain unless an explicit mapping and uncertainty bound is measured.
timing_mapping.freshness_rule: Existing F2 required_freshness_ns remains authoritative for scheduling/admission; backend queue timing is evidence feeding freshness diagnostics, not policy authority.

interaction_with_parallel_gstreamer_e1.separation: XDG/libportal/PipeWire supplies user-mediated session authorization, stream identity, narrowed remote and native buffer source; GStreamer E1 supplies optional queue/backpressure design patterns above/beside native ingestion.
interaction_with_parallel_gstreamer_e1.preferred_initial_stack: libportal session lifecycle + direct PipeWire stream + existing F2 bounded broker; do not add GStreamer unless later ablation shows its media negotiation/queue machinery provides measurable net value.

hypothesis.statement: A thin libportal + PipeWire host adapter can satisfy the missing Linux local screen-capture binding with stronger stale-session identity than node-id-based capture while preserving all existing F2 permission, generation, broker and authority boundaries.

counterhypothesis.statement: The adapter may still be too complex and brittle across compositor/portal/PipeWire backends; a GStreamer portal source or another mature wrapper may reduce integration bugs enough to outweigh the extra dependency and hidden buffering, provided it exposes exact session-close and pipewire-serial semantics.
counterhypothesis.falsifier: Before E5, run a deterministic E3 fixture against the proposed adapter state machine and, when an admitted local integration surface exists, compare a libportal+PipeWire prototype with one wrapper path on exact observables: ACTIVE/CLOSED transition, serial extraction, stale node-id reuse rejection, restore-with-new-serial generation bump, permission withdrawal behavior, bounded buffer handoff and cleanup.

next_fixture_cases: legacy node id reused while pipewire-serial changes -> stale binding rejected
same portal stream id restored with new serial -> F2 generation bump required
Session::Closed -> host grant invalid before next frame publication
restore token present after native permission withdrawal -> no host grant
PipeWire error/disconnect -> capture owner released before reopen
buffer from mismatched serial/generation -> no FrameRef publication
